A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoQD and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite additional appendices and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-task continuous-control experiments, BipedalWalker adaptation experiments, and embedding/descriptor dimensionality ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds weighting and rollout-count ablations, descriptor-stability measurements, additional comparisons, and qualitative behavior analyses.

M1.justification: The RFF trajectory embeddings, calibrated fitness-weighted PCA, affine descriptors, and alternating CMA-MAE procedure remain unchanged. The additional proofs and ablation variants do not replace the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six continuous-control tasks: Ant, HalfCheetah, Hopper, Swimmer, Walker2d, and BipedalWalker. BipedalWalker friction and mass variations are also retained; the new analyses reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds PGA-ME with hand-crafted descriptors to the detailed six-environment comparison in Table 8. The original RegularQD, Aurora, LSTM-Aurora, DvD-ES, and SMERL comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained, but substantial new evaluation protocols appear. These include successful-policy counts at 70%/90% return thresholds, descriptor stability using up to 100 policies per archive and 32 rollouts per policy, and 2/5/10-rollout controls. Table 8 adds maximum-fitness and archive-coverage measurements; the new adaptation box plots exclude negative returns.

E4.justification: The original dimensionality ablations are retained in Appendix H. v2 adds weighting ablation (Appendix C), descriptor-stability and rollout-count tests (Appendix I), quality-diversity and failure analyses (Appendix F), population-level adaptation analyses (Appendix G), and visual behavior case studies (Appendix J).

E5.justification: The new weighting comparison reports means and standard errors over eight seeds and introduces a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test, reporting p > 0.7. Existing three-seed benchmark/ablation reporting and Figure 3's 32 evaluation seeds remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 and the original dimensionality-ablation results are unchanged. v2 adds extensive results in Tables 3, 8, and 9 and new diagnostic figures. For example, Table 9 reports GT QD scores of 5.99, 6.09, and 6.12 × 10^4 for 2, 5, and 10 rollouts; these compare different settings, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A corrects RFF coordinate bounds and replaces part of the concentration argument with McDiarmid's inequality. New Appendix B develops lemmas and bounds for trajectory-averaged embeddings, including a finite-horizon error term of 2√2γ^T. The occupancy-measure correspondence is also qualified for Markovian policies in fully observable MDPs.

C1.justification: The four central contributions remain. However, the abstract and introduction replace broad off-the-shelf or seamless QD-integration language with explicit emphasis on CMA-MAE and black-box QD, qualifying the practical integration claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of premature convergence to stable, simple behaviors, possible drawbacks of fitness weighting, and quality-diversity trade-offs. It distinguishes adaptation by a successful subset from robustness of the entire population and discusses instability when combining changing descriptors with gradient-based QD.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies an AutoQD source-code link. v2 also documents procedures for the new diagnostics and qualitative selection, including filtering the top 20% of policies and selecting diverse candidates. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against human-feedback QD through Ding et al. and references supporting extinction events, evolutionary optimization limitations, and the expanded concentration analysis. The overall positioning against unsupervised QD and skill-discovery methods remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain recognizable, with tightened prose, terminology edits, and author-year citations. The closing section becomes Conclusion, and acknowledgments and an AI-use statement are added. Existing appendices are renumbered around the new material.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial visual evidence: weighting and rollout tables, a detailed benchmark table, trade-off and adaptation-distribution plots, descriptor-variance plots, and behavior sequences. Existing Figures 1–3 and dimensionality plots are retained or relocated; the document also adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through component ablations, descriptor-stability tests, population-level adaptation analysis, and inspectable behavior examples, addressing gaps in v1's mostly aggregate evidence. Expanded limitations and code-access information further improve transparency. These gains outweigh localized reporting errors, including Appendix F crediting SMERL with the five maximum-fitness wins that Table 8 shows for PGA-ME. The theoretical treatment improves but remains incomplete: the retained inequality in Eq. (36) does not justify the probability bound in Eq. (37).
